name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to Impaired Androgen Production
aliases: 46,XY Disorder of Sex Development with Impaired Androgen Synthesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for 46,XY DSD due to Androgen Biosynthesis Defect

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in androgen biosynthesis (e.g., HSD17B3, SRD5A2)
Presence of ambiguous genitalia or undervirilization in a 46,XY individual at birth
Biochemical evidence of impaired androgen production including low serum testosterone and elevated precursor steroids
Imaging evidence of testes in typical or ectopic locations
Normal mineralocorticoid function to exclude adrenal insufficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ambiguous genitalia or undervirilization in a 46,XY individual plus biochemical evidence of impaired androgen production and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants in androgen biosynthesis genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including endocrinology, genetics, and radiology.

searchTerms: ambiguous external sex organs with micropenis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypospadias with varying degrees of severity
searchTerms: urethral opening defect of varying severity

common.symptomName: Delayed or incomplete virilization at puberty
Reduced facial and body hair growth
searchTerms: less facial and body hair growth

occasional.notes: Reported in some cases with associated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
searchTerms: reduced or lost sense of smell
small male breast growth in childhood

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to gender ambiguity
searchTerms: emotional problems due to ambiguous genitalia

occasional.symptomName: Mild skeletal abnormalities such as delayed bone age

searchTerms: high blood pressure from adrenal enlargement
hypertension due to adrenal gland problem
blood pressure raised by adrenal hyperplasia

rare.symptomName: Severe electrolyte imbalance due to adrenal insufficiency
rare.notes: Rarely present if adrenal steroidogenesis is also impaired

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric disorders including depression and anxiety

laboratory: Low serum testosterone levels in infancy and puberty
Elevated serum androstenedione and other androgen precursors
Normal or elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing presence and location of testes
Absence of Müllerian structures on pelvic imaging
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HSD17B3, SRD5A2, or other androgen biosynthesis genes
other: Histological confirmation of testicular tissue if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Normal or elevated serum testosterone with resistance to androgen action
Absent or sparse pubic and axillary hair

redFlags: Severe ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent multidisciplinary evaluation
Signs of adrenal crisis or salt-wasting
Rapid virilization in infancy or childhood
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Ahmed SF, et al. UK guidance on the initial evaluation of ambiguous genitalia. Arch Dis Child. 2010.
Orphanet: 46,XY difference of sex development due to impaired androgen production. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
